title: How to prevent Electron safeStorage decryption errors from deleting API keys
summary:
📝 Originally published (in Japanese) at forge.workstyle.tech.

TL;DR A screen check script used the same settings location as the Electron app and handled ciphertext with a differently signed executable. Decryption then failed, and the error handler deleted all four API keys. Keep unreadable ciphertext under another name, retry it on read, and keep the check script away from getSettings() and safeStorage.

title: France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack
summary:
Interesting:

U.S. intelligence agencies have recently reached a “”ow confidence” assessment that Iran was responsible for the attacks in France, according to three U.S. officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive intelligence. A “low confidence” assessment generally means that there is some intelligence that points in a certain direction but is fragmented, and that the assessment could change as more information is collected.

The agencies’ judgment on the French incidents linked those attacks to Iran generally and not to a specific group such as the Revolutionary Guards, two of the officials said. They added that Iran was also seen as probably responsible for other similar attacks around Europe, but that those investigations were in their early stages...

title: External sandboxes for coding agents
summary:
External sandboxes for coding agents

I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine.

I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects.

My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
summary:
AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

title: Resetting Vue State When Related Converter Routes Reuse One Component
summary:
Moving between two converter URLs does not necessarily mean Vue creates a fresh component instance. I'll use a feet-to-meters page to show how to reset reused input refs without letting two-way watchers overwrite the intended defaults.

I used a feet-to-meters page as a concrete example. The arithmetic is simply multiplication by 0.3048, but the implementation is more interesting as a small case study in route-driven data, editable state, and resetting both sides of a two-way calculation.

Put Page Identity in Route Data

The application describes fixed conversion pairs as data. Each pair carries a slug, category, source unit, destination unit, development-order value, and localized content.

The router expands those definitions into routes that use one shared component. It places the pair slug in route metadata, so the component can look up the current definition:
